title: Grade 9 Mathematics — Circles
description: Circle properties — chords, arcs, central and inscribed angles, cyclic quadrilaterals
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A chord of a circle is:
options: A line tangent to the circle
A line segment joining two points on the circle
The distance from the centre to the circle (radius)
A line passing through the centre
questions.explanation: A chord is a line segment with both endpoints on the circle. The longest chord is the diameter (passing through the centre). A radius is NOT a chord.

questions.question: Equal chords of a circle are equidistant from the:
questions.explanation: Theorem: Equal chords of a circle are equidistant from the centre. Conversely, chords equidistant from the centre are equal. The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord.

questions.question: The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is _____ the angle subtended at any point on the remaining arc.
questions.explanation: Central Angle Theorem: The angle at the centre = 2 × angle at the circumference (inscribed angle). So central angle = double the inscribed angle subtended by the same arc.

questions.question: Angles in the same segment of a circle are:
questions.explanation: Theorem: All angles inscribed in the same segment of a circle (subtended by the same arc) are equal. This is the 'angles in the same segment' theorem.

questions.question: The angle in a semicircle (angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circle) is always:
questions.explanation: Thales' theorem: the angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circle is always 90°. This is a special case of the central angle theorem (diameter = arc of 180°, so inscribed angle = 90°).

questions.question: In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are:
questions.explanation: In a cyclic quadrilateral (all vertices lie on a circle), opposite angles are supplementary: ∠A + ∠C = 180° and ∠B + ∠D = 180°. This is the cyclic quadrilateral theorem.

questions.question: If the central angle of a minor arc is 80°, the central angle of the corresponding major arc is:
questions.explanation: Major arc + minor arc = full circle = 360°. If minor arc has central angle 80°, the major arc has central angle 360° − 80° = 280°.

questions.question: A line that touches a circle at exactly one point is called a:
questions.explanation: A tangent is a line that touches the circle at exactly one point (the point of tangency). A secant intersects the circle at two points. The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

questions.question: The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord:
options: Passes through the end of the chord
questions.explanation: Theorem: The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord (divides it into two equal parts). Conversely, the perpendicular bisector of any chord passes through the centre.

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, the central angle ∠AOB = 120°. The inscribed angle ∠APB (P on the major arc) is:
questions.explanation: By the Central Angle Theorem: inscribed angle = ½ × central angle. When P is on the MAJOR arc, the inscribed angle = ½ × 120° = 60°.

questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with ∠A = 70°. Find ∠C.
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary: ∠A + ∠C = 180°. ∠C = 180° − 70° = 110°.

questions.question: How many circles can pass through three non-collinear points?
questions.explanation: Through any three non-collinear points, exactly one circle can be drawn. This is because the perpendicular bisectors of the three segments joining the points meet at a unique centre.

questions.question: The area of a circle with radius 7 cm is: (use π = 22/7)
A chord AB of a circle is 16 cm long. The perpendicular from centre O to AB has length 6 cm. Find the radius of the circle.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular from centre bisects chord: half-chord = 8 cm. By Pythagoras: r² = 8² + 6² = 64 + 36 = 100. r = 10 cm.

questions.question: In the same circle, two chords are equal if and only if they subtend equal angles at:
questions.explanation: Theorem: In the same circle (or congruent circles), equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre. Conversely, chords that subtend equal angles at the centre are equal.
